questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

They would have / won the race / if they would have / run faster.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'if they would have'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'if they had' **should be used instead of** 'if they would have'.**
 
• The given sentence is an example of the **third conditional.**

 
• Third Conditional: The third conditional, also called the "Past Unreal" conditional is used to describe unreal situations in the past. It is often used to express regret about the past because the hypothetical situation that it describes is now impossible as a consequence of another past action. 
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is "If+Subject+had+V3, S+would+have+V3".​
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *If I had seen you, I would have stopped my car. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
• *If I had seen you, I would had stopped my car. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
 
 
• *​*Thus, the correct answer is** Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *They would have won the race **if they had **run faster.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

The joint family system __have undergone__ drastic changes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'has undergone'.**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'has undergone' **should be used instead of** 'have undergone'.**
 
• If** a collective noun** refers to a single subject we use **a singular helping verb.**
 
• A collective noun is a word or phrase that refers to a group of people or things as one entity.
 
 
• *Example: Every morning, **the herd **follows its leader to the watering hole for a drink.* → Herd is a singular collective noun. Follows is a singular verb, and the word its is a singular pronoun.
 
 
 
• **'The joint family system'** refers to a singular** collective noun. **Hence, '**has**' should be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The joint family system** has undergone **drastic changes.*
